questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Exciting culture and food, country in EU, beautiful nature with nice hiking trails, enough courses to choose from in english (that interest me)

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I had no problem with it I found a nice place in a good neighbourhood, big room with a small terasse. Very nice. Expensive too, but housing in Milan is expensive. I didn't want to stress too much about it and risk not finding something better/cheaper - so i just booked it quite early, and then I had peace of mind. 
I recommend finding a place that is specifically made for students/ erasmus /young people. Then you easily make new friends. Try to not live with people from your own country - you will meet them anyways.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Think about what area of town you live in, and how far away from city center it is. Transportation at night can be problematic, if it is very far away.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: On the website, they give you a guide. Take the time to sit down, read it through and then figure out which courses you want. They are also quite flexible, so you can change them later.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't stress too much about it, it will work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: very chill classes and exams. Not a big workload at all - but I did prioritize "easier" courses with less workload and oral exams (because they are super comfortable and unproblematic)

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer:
Courses were interesting, they were only 6 ects each, didn't have to study much for it at all. Basically didn't read ony texts to prepare for classes. I just showed up (attendance was mandatory in most courses). Exams were the most chill ever. Just a conversation with the professor in front of the class. But the professors were all super nice and they knew we were Erasmus students, so they went easy on us. I recommend to choose oral exams over written ones. In most courses at the end, you can make the choice yourself on what you prefer. And there will be several dates to choose from, so you can structure your own exam-plan as you want.
I didn't study more than 2-3 days for each exam, and they went well still.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Power Point Presentations, not super dynamic, not a lot of student participation. Just some questions, thats it. Basically no group work.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Definetly Smart Cities, Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation Law. Do your self the favor and choose this course. Low workload. But super interesting. Dedicated professor. Best structured class I had. Not a lot of classes actually, only once per week. And exam was super chill too - just a written paper, we could use the internet and Chatgpt for it.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: drink spritz just at the bars in front of the school. (cost 3 euro for one spritz!!!) lots of local students here. Be brave, talk to them.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Get ready to spend a lot of money, travel on the weekends, eat as much good food as you can - just enjoy it all!! (anything pistacchio-flavored is amazing)

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: loved it all. So many nice people. Amazing weather (so much sunshine compared to DK), nature was incredible, so many nice hiking areas.
